pages.text: This is Cloud. Cloud is a grey cat. She lives in the courtyard.

pages.text: Every afternoon, Cloud walks along the wall. Step, step, step.

pages.text: Today Cloud jumps down. Hop! Step, step, step… she comes close.

pages.text: Then Cloud stands up. Step, step, step… to the sunny corner. “Bye, Cloud,” says Ella.

activity.title: The Feel Bag
activity.goal: Name how things feel: soft, rough, smooth, squishy.
materials: A cloth bag with no drawstring
A smooth stone, bigger than the child’s fist

steps.caption: Four things go in the bag.

activity.safety: Check for allergies first (the pinecone is plant material). Everything is bigger than the child’s fist and nothing goes in the mouth. Take the sponge or pinecone away if it is chewed or breaks into bits. No drawstring on the bag. If there is an accident, call your local emergency number.
activity.forAdult: In the story, Ella learns a soft, slow hand for Cloud the cat. Being gentle starts with noticing how things feel, and this game gives the child the words for it. Put the four things in the bag. The child reaches in, holds one thing and feels it. Ask “How does it feel?” and wait a moment before you help with the word: soft, rough, smooth or squishy. Then the child pulls it out to check, and you say the word together. Stroke the woolly hat slowly and say “Soft hand, slow hand”, just like Ella. Then swap: you feel, and the child asks. To make it easier, use only two things that feel very different, such as the hat and the stone. To make it harder, ask the child to guess the thing before pulling it out (“Is it the stone?”). Five to ten minutes is plenty. Wash hands afterwards if you used things from outside.
activity.inClass: Sit in a small circle: one adult with up to four children. The bag goes round the circle. Each child feels one thing, says a word for it, and pulls it out to check while everyone says the word together. The thing goes back in the bag for the next child.
